name: O2C
tagline: Turning customer orders into cash through credit, billing, collections and banking control.
pickerIntro: Eight processes covering credit risk, sales orders, billing, collections, disputes, cash application and banking.

context.label: Solutions
context.text: Python scripts now automate Alexion order processing (returns and rebates), advance-payment clearing for China and Korea, China tax receipt journals for BlackLine and credit-control parameter extraction; a Global CN dashboard and Crown manual-payment simplification are in progress.

context.label: Automation
context.text: High Radius sends statements and reminders and auto-matches cash to invoices; SAP creates orders from daily EDI feeds, releases billing, runs the automated payment run and posts MT940 / CAMT53 bank statements.

context.label: AI
context.text: An AI solution for the credit review process is underway, alongside an agentic AI solution to match credit-limit changes to supporting emails; neither is documented as deployed yet.

context.label: Cross-Functional Collaboration
context.text: O2C relies on the Distribution team and DMT for EDI account and stock fixes, local markets, FP&A and GFS Controlling for pricing, credit approvals and forecasts, Key Account Managers and Finance Controllers for collection escalations, and GBS, Controlling and the banks for payments and reconciliations.

processes.title: Credit risk management
processes.purpose:
Credit risk management assesses and approves the credit extended to customers so that sales orders can be released without exposing AZ to undue default risk. It covers new customer credit risk assessment at on-boarding, periodic review of existing customers based on their next review date, credit limit utilisation monitoring, release of credit-held orders, investigation of D&B risk alerts and monthly controls.

The outputs are an approved credit limit (or a credit limit increase or decrease), a risk rating or score, and where necessary an account placed on hold or blocked.
processes.cadence: Risk alerts arrive daily from D&B and the utilisation report is shared weekly with MC. Periodic reviews of existing customers are based on the next review date; for Europe and Alexion new customers, smaller default credit limits are reviewed again after six months and larger limits in the next annual cycle. Monthly controls run each month. New-customer reviews, credit-held orders and ad hoc MC requests are handled as they arise.

stages.title: Review new customer credit
stages.detail:
New customers
1. New customer reviews are triggered through our internal report for new customers, ad hoc MC requests, or credit-held sales orders.
2. The issue is where the customer can start before a CL is assigned, therefore leading to blocked orders. We have on-going discussion with the market about subject to credit (STC).
3. All markets follow an appropriate review process based on the size of the credit limit. However, in Europe and Alexion, a default credit limit and risk category are assigned to new customers due to volumes and blocking considerations. This process is managed by DMT. Smaller credit limits are reviewed again in six months to assess payment experience, while larger limits are reviewed in the next annual cycle.
4. For new customers with credit-held orders, the review is completed and the order release team is informed whether the order can be released.
stages.owner: Credit risk team (DMT for Europe / Alexion default limits)
challenges: New customer process for Europe / Alexion: material volume (around 3K a year); using GDM to complete the reviews is still effort.
stages.displayTitle: Review new customer credit
stages.description:
New customer reviews are triggered by the internal new-customer report, ad hoc MC requests or credit-held sales orders. A known on-boarding issue is that a customer can start trading before a credit limit is assigned, which leads to blocked orders; discussions with the market about subject-to-credit (STC) are ongoing.

All markets follow a review process appropriate to the size of the credit limit. In Europe and Alexion, a default credit limit and risk category are assigned to new customers because of volumes and blocking considerations; this process is managed by DMT. Smaller credit limits are reviewed again after six months to assess payment experience, while larger limits are reviewed in the next annual cycle.

For new customers with credit-held orders, the review is completed and the order release team is informed whether the order can be released.

stages.displayTitle: Assess existing customers and select review type
stages.description: On the periodic review cycle (based on each account's next review date), the credit analyst reviews the accounts in their market, checks the customer's credit profile and determines whether a simple review (credit limit below $1M) or a full review (credit limit above $1M) is required.

stages.title: Complete simple reviews in Global Decision Maker
stages.detail: 2. Simple review process is completed through the Global Decision Maker (GDM). GDM is a semi-automated application to accelerate accurate credit risk decision in real time through a blend of scoring methodology which includes D&B risk band (failure score, paydex etc) & AZ payment experience (ageing, DSO).
stages.displayTitle: Complete simple reviews in Global Decision Maker
stages.description: Simple reviews are completed through the Global Decision Maker (GDM), a semi-automated application that accelerates accurate credit risk decisions in real time. GDM blends a scoring methodology that combines the D&B risk band (failure score, paydex and similar measures) with AZ payment experience (ageing and DSO).

stages.title: Perform full reviews and obtain DOA 2002 approval
stages.detail: 3. Full reviews require validation of customer information (a limited KYC is done at market level) and supporting documents such as sales forecasts, financial statements, payment term changes, and contracts where needed, followed by an assessment of sales trends, financial position, ageing, DSO, country risk, and D&B criteria. We will perform a deep dive into the customer's financials and assess the customer's credit worthiness against the credit limit required.  A credit proposal is then submitted by email with supporting documents for multi-level approval under DOA 2002 (up to Group CFO) after which the data team updates the relevant credit details in SAP via service now ticketing system.
stages.owner: Credit analyst; data team for the SAP update
challenges: Sales forecast: the team does not receive forecasts at customer level with monthly phasing, nor does it have access to the approved budget submission. It relies on the markets / FP&A to provide the forecast, which is time consuming.
Manual credit review process: financial spreading, financial analysis, proposal write-up and approvals.
stages.displayTitle: Perform full reviews and obtain DOA 2002 approval
stages.description:
Full reviews start with validation of the customer information (a limited KYC is done at market level) and collection of supporting documents such as sales forecasts, financial statements, payment term changes and contracts where needed. The analyst then assesses sales trends, financial position, ageing, DSO, country risk and D&B criteria, performing a deep dive into the customer's financials to judge creditworthiness against the credit limit required.

A credit proposal is submitted by email with the supporting documents for multi-level approval under DOA 2002 (up to Group CFO). Once approved, the data team updates the relevant credit details in SAP via a ServiceNow ticket.

stages.title: Monitor credit limit utilisation
stages.detail:
Monitor credit limit utilization
1. A weekly utilization report is shared with MC, highlighting customers above 80% or 90% of their credit limit to prevent blocked orders.
2. Based on MC feedback, the credit analyst performs a review where a limit increase is required, for example due to sales growth or new product launches.
stages.displayTitle: Monitor credit limit utilisation

Based on MC feedback, the credit analyst performs a review where a limit increase is required, for example because of sales growth or new product launches.

stages.title: Review and release credit-held orders
stages.detail:
Credit held order management
1. Depending on the value, the credit risk team would need to review the customer for an increased credit limit before the blocked order is manually released.
2. Credit-blocked orders must follow the global credit risk standard before manual release. If blocked due to insufficient credit limit, payment status may be confirmed with collections, and if payment is received in the AZ bank statement, the order can be released without approval. If there is no payment found, the order can be manually released if approved in line with GDOA 2002 based on the customer's total exposure including the order value.
3. If an order is blocked due to overdue, the collection team must be informed and ensure that the relevant approvals according to the matrix in the credit risk standard (who can release it based on value and overdue allowance) before release.
4. Where an order is blocked due to payment terms (order PT being different to SAP PT), the order value must be checked and approval obtained from MC following the DOA 2000 before any modifications made to the PT in the sales order and address any other credit related issues before releasing the order.
5. Alexion orders are not blocked in the system due to its life-saving nature.
stages.owner: Credit risk team, with Collections and MC approvals
challenges: Blocked orders: Greece cash in advance (CIA) customers are blocked due to legacy practice.
stages.displayTitle: Review and release credit-held orders
stages.description:
Depending on the order value, the credit risk team may need to review the customer for an increased credit limit before a blocked order is released manually. Credit-blocked orders must follow the global credit risk standard before manual release.

If the block is due to an insufficient credit limit, payment status may be confirmed with Collections: if payment has been received in the AZ bank statement the order can be released without approval, otherwise it can be released manually only if approved in line with GDOA 2002 based on the customer's total exposure including the order value. If the block is due to overdue balances, the collection team must be informed and the relevant approvals obtained according to the matrix in the credit risk standard (who can release based on value and overdue allowance).

Where an order is blocked because its payment terms differ from the SAP payment terms, the order value must be checked and approval obtained from MC under DOA 2000 before the payment terms on the sales order are modified; any other credit-related issues are addressed before release. Alexion orders are not blocked in the system because of their life-saving nature.

stages.title: Investigate daily D&B risk alerts
stages.detail:
Risk alerts investigation
1. The team receives daily D&B alerts covering legal events, rating changes, ownership changes, and customer name changes across active global customers.
2. The objective of alerts process is for the team to identify potential credit risk / defaults.
3. Based on alerts received the credit risk team will take the necessary action or trigger an ad hoc credit review. When a credit event occurs e.g. bankruptcy and ceased trading, this is considered high priority, and the team would deactivate the customer where necessary.
stages.displayTitle: Investigate daily D&B risk alerts
stages.description:
The team receives daily D&B alerts covering legal events, rating changes, ownership changes and customer name changes across active global customers. The objective is to identify potential credit risk or defaults early.

Based on the alerts received, the credit risk team takes the necessary action or triggers an ad hoc credit review. A credit event such as bankruptcy or ceased trading is treated as high priority, and the team deactivates the customer where necessary.

TPI 2026 (completed): Implemented a Python solution for extraction of control parameters, working file and remarks.

processes.title: Sales order management
processes.purpose:
Sales order management creates sales orders in SAP from three inputs: daily EDI sales reports interfaced by distributors, customers' purchase orders for manual orders, and customers' returns and rebate settlements. It resolves EDI errors with the Distribution, DMT, local market and GFS Controlling teams, applies the system credit check to manual orders, routes blocked orders to the right approver and creates credit notes for approved returns and rebates.

The output is a created sales order, which feeds delivery and billing.
processes.cadence: Distributors interface daily EDI sales reports to SAP, so EDI order creation runs daily. Manual orders, returns and rebate credit notes are processed as customer purchase orders and settlement requests are received.

stages.title: Create sales orders from daily EDI reports
stages.detail:
a) EDI: daily sales reports which are interfaced by Distributors to AZ's SAP
EDI (sales and returns)
1. SAP automatically creates sales orders based on the daily EDI report which interfaced by distributors.
challenges: EDI interface risk related to deliveries spanning across month-end.
stages.displayTitle: Create sales orders from daily EDI reports
stages.description: Distributors interface their daily sales reports (sales and returns) to AZ's SAP through EDI. SAP automatically creates the corresponding sales orders from each daily EDI report.

stages.title: Resolve EDI errors with the relevant teams
stages.detail:
2. When system identifies an error, the Sales Order team reviews the issue and follows up with the relevant teams to resolve the EDI errors.
a) For a missing end-customer account, the team liaises with the Distribution team to submit a request to DMT for account creation.
b) For missing pricing, the team liaises with the local market and GFS Controlling team to update the pricing details.
c) For insufficient stock, the team liaises with the Distribution team to carry out the necessary stock movements.
challenges: EDI errors arising from missing end-customer accounts, missing pricing and insufficient stock.
stages.displayTitle: Resolve EDI errors with the relevant teams
stages.description:
When the system identifies an error in the EDI feed, the Sales Order team reviews the issue and follows up with the relevant teams to resolve it.

For a missing end-customer account, the team liaises with the Distribution team to submit a request to DMT for account creation. For missing pricing, the team liaises with the local market and the GFS Controlling team to update the pricing details. For insufficient stock, the team liaises with the Distribution team to carry out the necessary stock movements.

stages.title: Validate and create manual sales orders
stages.detail:
b) Customer's purchase order
Manual order (sales)
The Sales Order team validates the completeness of the data and manually creates the order in SAP.
Orders are then subjected to a system credit check. The system will block an order if the customer account has an insufficient credit limit or overdue outstanding balances.
challenges: Manual creation of sales orders.
Incorrect price or VAT classification in the master data, resulting in inaccurate invoicing.

Local markets have signed contracts with customers that include non-standard payment terms or multiple payment terms for a single customer, or without confirming whether the system can support them, which has created challenges for O2C in processing sales orders.
stages.displayTitle: Validate and create manual sales orders
stages.description:
For manual orders, the Sales Order team validates the completeness of the data on the customer's purchase order and manually creates the order in SAP.

Orders are then subjected to a system credit check. The system blocks an order if the customer account has an insufficient credit limit or overdue outstanding balances.
stages.challengeScope: Process-wide challenge; the source does not assign it to an individual step.

stages.title: Route credit-blocked orders for approval
stages.detail:
If an order is blocked:
a) For blocks due to credit limit exceeded, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance with GDOA 2002.
b) For blocks due to overdue balances, the Collection team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance to Global Credit Risk Policy.
c) For blocks due to a change in payment term, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance with GDOA 2000.
challenges: High volume of order blocks in CNXX markets.
stages.displayTitle: Route credit-blocked orders for approval
stages.description: If an order is blocked, the reason for the block determines who reviews it. For blocks due to the credit limit being exceeded, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance with GDOA 2002. For blocks due to overdue balances, the Collection team reviews the case and obtains approval in accordance with the Global Credit Risk Policy. For blocks due to a change in payment terms, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains approval in accordance with GDOA 2000.

stages.title: Create credit notes for approved returns and rebates
stages.detail:
c) Customer's returns, rebates settlement
Manual order (returns, rebates)
The Sales Order team verifies whether the appropriate approvals for returns and rebate requests have been obtained before creating the credit notes.
stages.displayTitle: Create credit notes for approved returns and rebates
stages.description: For customer returns and rebate settlements, the Sales Order team verifies that the appropriate approvals for the return or rebate request have been obtained before creating the credit notes.

challenges: EDI errors arising from missing end-customer accounts, missing pricing and insufficient stock.
Manual creation of sales orders.
Incorrect price or VAT classification in the master data, resulting in inaccurate invoicing.
High volume of order blocks in CNXX markets.
EDI interface risk related to deliveries spanning across month-end.

Local markets have signed contracts with customers that include non-standard payment terms or multiple payment terms for a single customer, or without confirming whether the system can support them, which has created challenges for O2C in processing sales orders.
improvements: TPI 2026 (completed): Developed a Python script to automate order processing for Alexion transactions, returns and rebates.
TPI 2026 (in progress): System change request to exclude Banker's Acceptance from the credit exposure calculation for CNXX markets (expected to go live in October).
TPI 2026 (in progress): Developing a Global CN Dashboard to provide insights and identify potential improvement opportunities.

processes.title: Delivery and billing
processes.purpose:
Delivery and billing turns a created sales order into a delivery and then into an invoice. The system creates the delivery order (automatically for EDI orders, or for the warehouse team to pick and pack for manual orders), posts the goods issue to record cost of goods sold, releases billing to enable revenue recognition and sends invoices to customers.

Where local rules require it, the Billing team prepares local tax invoices (for example in Vietnam and Korea) and, in countries that have implemented e-invoicing, sales data is submitted to the local tax authority. The outputs are the delivery and the invoices and credit notes.

stages.detail:
Manual order
1. The system generates the corresponding delivery order for the warehouse team to carry out the pick-and-pack process.
stages.displayTitle: Generate delivery orders for warehouse pick and pack
stages.description: For manual orders, the system generates the corresponding delivery order, which the warehouse team uses to carry out the pick-and-pack process.

stages.title: Post goods issue to record COGS
stages.detail: 2. The goods issue is posted to record the cost of goods sold (COGS). | Delivery
stages.displayTitle: Post goods issue to record COGS
stages.description: Once the goods leave the warehouse, the goods issue is posted to record the cost of goods sold (COGS). The delivery is the output of this step and the input to billing.

stages.title: Release billing and send invoices to customers
stages.detail:
Delivery | 1. The system automatically releases the billing to enable revenue recognition.
2. The system automatically send the invoices to customers.
stages.displayTitle: Release billing and send invoices to customers
stages.description: The system automatically releases billing on the delivery to enable revenue recognition, and automatically sends the invoices to customers. Invoices and credit notes are the output of this step.

stages.detail:
3. For certain markets such as Vietnam and Korea, the Billing team prepares the local tax invoice.
4. For countries that have implemented e-invoicing, the sales data is submitted to the local tax authority.

For countries that have implemented e-invoicing, the sales data is submitted to the local tax authority as mandated by the local government.

Collection management secures payment of the invoices and credit notes billed to customers. It issues statements of account and pre-due reminders, follows up with customers before the invoice due date, escalates customers that will not commit to a payment, and ensures that any payment hold requested by a customer is approved by the local market.

The output is payment collection from the customer.

processes.title: Dispute management
processes.purpose:
Dispute management handles disputed invoices and short payments. The Collection team validates the customer's claim with the relevant stakeholders and resolves it through a credit note, an invoice correction or a rejection where the claim is invalid, and records every dispute in High Radius and SAP so that disputed items are excluded from the system credit check.

The outputs are payment collection from the customer, credit note issuance or invoice correction.
processes.cadence: Triggered when a customer disputes an invoice or deducts a claim from a payment (short payment).

stages.title: Review and validate disputed invoices
stages.detail: 1.If a customer disputes an invoice, the Collection team will review the dispute details and validate them with the relevant stakeholders to resolve the issue through credit notes, invoice corrections, or dispute rejection if the claim is found to be invalid.
challenges: The team spends significant time and effort following up with the relevant teams to investigate and resolve disputes.
stages.displayTitle: Review and validate disputed invoices
stages.description: If a customer disputes an invoice, the Collection team reviews the dispute details and validates them with the relevant stakeholders. The issue is resolved through a credit note, an invoice correction, or rejection of the dispute if the claim is found to be invalid.

stages.title: Investigate customer deductions from payments
stages.detail: 2. When a customer deducts claims such as returns, rebates, or AP due invoices from the payment made to AZ, the Collection team will obtain the relevant details from the customer, follow up as needed, and validate the deduction with the appropriate stakeholders for resolution or rejection if the claim is determined to be invalid.
challenges: Customers often deduct claim amounts from payments before a credit note (CN) is issued.
stages.displayTitle: Investigate customer deductions from payments

stages.title: Record disputes in High Radius and SAP
stages.detail: 3. All disputes are recorded in the High Radius Collection system and SAP to ensure that disputed items are excluded from the system credit check.
stages.displayTitle: Record disputes in High Radius and SAP
stages.description: All disputes are recorded in the High Radius Collection system and in SAP so that disputed items are excluded from the system credit check.

challenges: The team spends significant time and effort following up with the relevant teams to investigate and resolve disputes.
Customers often deduct claim amounts from payments before a credit note (CN) is issued.

processes.title: Cash application
processes.purpose:
Cash application clears customer payments against the corresponding invoices in the customer accounts. Daily bank statements flow into the High Radius Cash Application (HRC) system, which matches payments to invoices using the remittance advice or rules configured in the system and interfaces the results to SAP. Some manual intervention remains for exceptions such as withholding tax deductions.

The output is payments cleared against the corresponding invoices in the customer accounts.

processes.title: Payments (cash and banking)
processes.purpose:
The Cash & Banking payments process makes payments to vendors and other payees from two inputs: vendor postings settled through the automated SAP payment run, and manual payment requests raised through Crown (including customer refunds). The team reconciles payment runs against the bank acknowledgement, investigates failures, and validates and processes manual payments through the FIS Payment Hub or the bank portal.

The output is payments successfully made to vendors.
